answer: Per-network minting caps: in each epoch one autonomous system or /24 block may sponsor only a handful of new identities, and every registration carries a path fingerprint: traceroute shape, TTL, and latency jitter measured across a horizon of vantage points. Fingerprints that land in the same umber band of the histogram are merged into one voting weight, so a farm streaking in like comets from a single datacenter uplink still counts exactly once. The attacker must rent many genuinely separate uplinks and keep each alive, so cost scales with real network diversity, not with CPU.
